 This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice C.M. Poonacha
 Oral Judgment
The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 19881
challenging the judgment and award dated 24.03.2015 passed in MVC.No.77/2012 by the Senior
Civil Judge and C.J.M, and Member of Mact2., Chamarajanagar, seeking for enhancement of
compensation.
2.  The Tribunal vide its judgment and award dated 24.03.2015 has partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a compensation of `2,08,900/- together with interest at 6% per annum.
Being aggrieved, the claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation has filed the present appeal.
Hereinafter referred as to 'Act' Hereinafter referred as to 'Tribunal' NC: 2025:KHC:25231 HC-KAR 3.
The findings of the Tribunal on negligence and liability are not under challenge and have attained finality.
Hence, the only aspect to be adjudicated upon in the present appeal is with regard to the adequacy of compensation awarded.

4. Heard submissions of learned counsel Sri Manjunatha.N.D., appearing for the appellant - claimant and learned counsel Smt.H.R.Renuka appearing for the respondent.
5.
The claimant was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident i.e., as on 12.07.2012.

Hence the Tribunal has rightly applied the appropriate multiplier of 18.
6.
It was averred that the claimant was working as a mason and earning `9,000/- per month.
However, no documents have been produced to demonstrate the income.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the claimant as `5,000/- p.m.
However, having with regard to the date of the accident, the notional income of the claimant is re
- assessed as `7,000/- per month.

sentences.text: It is forthcoming from the wound certificate (Ex.P.5) and the other medical evidence available on record that the claimants sustained fracture of left femur as well as other simple injuries.
Claimant was treated as in-patient for a total period of 10 days.
The Doctor was examined as CW.1 and he has deposed that the disability at 8% of the limb.

The Tribunal has re-assessed the disability at 3%,
which is just and proper.
8. Having regard to the aforementioned the quantum of compensation is re-
assessed as follows:
8.1. The Tribunal has awarded medical expenses as per the actual bills in sum of `1,11,500/-, which is just and proper.

Hence, the same is rounded of `1,12,000/-;
8.2.

The Tribunal has awarded `10,000/- towards food, nourishment, diet and attendant charges as well as `5,000/- towards conveyance charges which is just and proper;
8.3.
The Tribunal has assessed the laid up period as one month and awarded `5,000/- towards loss of earning during the period of treatment.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained and the period of treatment, the compensation towards pain and suffering is re

- assessed `30,000/- as against `20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal;
8.5.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards future medical expenses of `25,000/- which is not interfered with;
8.6.

The compensation awarded towards loss of future earning capacity/disability is re-assessed as (7000X12X18X3%) = `45,360/-;
8.7.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, the loss of amenities is re
- assessed as `15,000/-.

Hence, the compensation is re
- assessed as follows;

Towards loss of earning 5,000.00 21,000.00 during the period of treatment 4
Towards pain and 20,000.00 30,000.00 suffering 5
Towards loss of future 32,400.00 45,360.00 earning on account of permanent disability 6.

For conveyance charges 5,000.00 5,000.00 Ningaraju vs Divisional Controller on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85380909/
3 7.
For future medical 25,000.00 25,000.00 expenses 8. Loss of amenities NIL 15,000.00 TOTAL 2,08,900.00 2,63,360.00 10.

Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of (`2,63,360/- -
`2,08,900/-) = `54,460/-, rounded of `55,000/-.
Having regard to the order dated 10.12.2018 the claimant shall not be entitled for interest for the delayed period of 507 days.
12. Taking judicial notice of the rate of interest awarded towards fixed deposits, the rate of interest on the enhanced compensation is re-assessed as 7% per annum.
In all other respects, the judgment and award of the Tribunal remains unaltered;
Upon deposit of compensation together with accrued interest, the same shall be digitally released to the claimant.

v) The Registry to draw the modified award accordingly;
vi) Records of the Tribunal be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
No costs.
